lead: The 2027 manager does not manage only people. Agents, models, processes, tools, permissions, context, knowledge and compute budget all pass across their desk. Most of these objects already exist in your company and have no owner. In this lesson you build the map of the nine, with a name next to each one, and find out which course in the program looks after which.
objetivo: list the 9 management objects that pass across the 2027 manager's desk and give each one an owner with a name in your area.

aprende.t: The nine management objects, grouped into four axes and two cross-cutting themes
The difference between who answers for the object and who keeps it running
The invisible objects: context, knowledge, permissions and budget
Which course in the program takes care of each object

hero_alt: A manager points to a whiteboard with colored sticky notes in a three-by-three grid, with nothing written on them; two colleagues watch from their seats.

secoes.titulo: Nine objects, four axes and two cross-cutting themes
secoes.sub: Each block is an axis; inside it are the objects it brings together and the course in the program that takes care of them. Tap to see the details.

nos.detalhe: The people on the team and what stays with them: decisions, relationships, exceptions, training for new hires. This is the first object and the one that changes shape the most: the junior who supervises agents, the load of exceptions, the conversation about fear.

The process stops being paper in a drawer and gets a version, like software. Before you put an agent on it, you take it apart: what exists out of habit, what exists because it is required, what only existed because there was no other way.

Each agent, with a role, a goal and authority limits, and the context it receives to do its work. Poorly kept context is the most common cause of an agent that "makes things up": it only knows what is written down.

itens.sub: in a form the agent reads

nos.detalhe: The resources that drive the agents: the model, the tools, the company's knowledge written in a way the agent can read, and the compute budget. The cost question changes from "how much does one call cost?" to "how much does it cost to produce the result?".
Who can do what, with which identity and which credential, and where the record is kept. It cuts across all the axes: a tool released with no owner becomes a permission with no owner.

It is not one of the nine objects: it is how the manager knows whether each one is doing well. Quality, time per task, cost per result, failures and rework, how much the agent did without stopping and how much human intervention it needed.

secoes.legenda: The nine objects come from the AI Management area of INEMA (section "The 2027 Manager"); the grouping into axes is the one from the AI Management Program 2027.

secoes.sub: Four ideas for building the map without falling into the most common traps. Horizonte is the fictional study company.

texto: The list of what crosses the manager's desk has grown: people, agents, models, processes, tools, permissions, context, knowledge and compute budget. You don't need to master each one technically. You need to know who answers for it.
An object with no owner doesn't sit still: someone decides for it without realizing it, almost always whoever has access to the system.

exemplo.texto: Nobody chose the model that powers Hora: Rafael used what came with the tool. When the price or the behavior changes, nobody will know they need to decide.

texto: Each object has two roles: who answers for the result and who keeps it running. IT maintains; the business answers. When both land on the same technical person, the business loses control without noticing.
The owner is always a name. "The team" or "IT" don't count: when everyone answers, no one answers.

exemplo.texto: In the official inventory, Rafael is responsible for 6 of the 8 tools, including Hora and the sales email assistant. Patrícia only appears as the owner of the spreadsheets.

texto: People and agents show up on any org chart. Context, knowledge, permissions and budget don't, and that's where the risk lives: customer data leaving the company, the tool that can delete, the cost nobody watches.
When you build the map, start with the invisible ones. They are the ones that most often show up as "no owner."

exemplo.texto: The service summary sends the conversations, with name, phone and CPF, to a free service outside Brazil (lab failure F10). And the email assistant can send and delete without approval (F9).

texto: Deloitte, in Tech Trends 2026, treats agents as a "silicon-based" workforce: they need integration with data and operations, graduated autonomy with human supervision triggers, and the human supervisors need training too.
This is one consultancy's view, not a measurement. But it confirms the logic of the map: an agent is a management object, with an owner, and whoever supervises it also needs to be prepared.

exemplo.texto: Nobody integrated Hora: it was just configured. And nobody prepared Patrícia to supervise it. The map shows both gaps on the same line.

secoes.titulo: Template to copy: the map of the 9 objects
secoes.sub: One page per area. Fill in what exists, today's owner and the right owner. Where there is no owner, write "no owner": it's the most useful information on the map.

blocos.conteudo:
You are an experienced manager reviewing the map of the 9 management objects of an
area that has started using AI agents. Don't fill anything in: point out gaps.

Map:
"""<paste here>"""

Answer, in this order:
1. On which lines is the "right owner" IT when it should be the business?
2. Is any owner "the team," "everyone" or a role with no name?
3. Of the invisible objects (context, knowledge, permissions, budget),
   which looks filled in without anyone really having looked?
4. What question would I ask each owner to find out whether they know they are the owner?

secoes.sub: Horizonte's map is for practice; your area's map is for real.
secoes.fonte: Lab materials: IT inventory, service summary and email assistant (fictional study company).

exercicios.texto: With the inventory and the two lab pieces open, fill in the map of the 9 objects for Horizonte's sales area without looking at the example. For each object, write today's owner (from the inventory) and the right owner. Then compare and note where you disagreed with the example and why.
exercicios.pronto: all nine lines are filled in, at least three objects show up as "no owner" today, every right owner is a name, and there is one sentence saying what the biggest risk is and why.

exercicios.texto: Make the map of your area. For the invisible objects (context, knowledge, permissions and budget), ask whoever maintains the systems before filling them in. Run the prompt and finish with the first decision: who takes which object, by when.
exercicios.pronto: the map has nine lines with a name or an acknowledged "no owner" on each one, at least one conversation with whoever maintains the systems, and a first decision with a name and a date.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: Which of these is NOT among the nine management objects?
perguntas.explica: The nine are people, agents, models, processes, tools, permissions, context, knowledge and compute budget. The org chart shows people; the invisible objects don't appear on it.

perguntas.p: In Horizonte's inventory, Rafael appears as the person responsible for Hora. What is wrong?
opcoes: Nothing: he's the one who set it up
He keeps the agent running, but the person who answers for the result (discount, customer) is on the business side: Patrícia
The person responsible should be the tool vendor
perguntas.explica: Who keeps it running and who answers for it are different roles. IT takes care of keeping it on; the business answers for the margin and the customer.

perguntas.p: Why start the map with the invisible objects?
opcoes: Because they are the most expensive
Because context, knowledge, permissions and budget don't show up on an org chart, and they are the ones most likely to have no owner
Because they are technical and IT has to fill them in first
perguntas.explica: That's where the risk nobody sees lives: customer data leaking out, a tool that deletes things, a cost with no owner. And the business decides about them, not just IT.

perguntas.p: Deloitte (Tech Trends 2026) calls agents a "silicon-based" workforce. How should you use that?
opcoes: As measured proof that agents replace people
As a consulting view that supports the logic: an agent needs integration, graduated autonomy and prepared supervisors
As a standard the company is required to follow
perguntas.explica: It's a view, not a measurement or a standard. Use it to show leadership that integrating the agent and preparing the people who supervise it are management tasks.

itens.texto: People, agents, models, processes, tools, permissions, context, knowledge, budget.
The business answers for it, IT keeps it running. An owner is a name.
Context, knowledge, permissions and budget are the ones that end up with no owner.
G1 people, G2 processes, G3 agents, G4 resources, G5 governance and evidence.
